title: The electoral map
hook: Electoral allocations do not measure the popular vote.
notes: Original Orbis factual synthesis; linked federal records and historic-site accounts, checked 14 October 2026. Points locate places approximately, not territorial extents. Modern national/state outlines are reference geography, never reconstructed historical borders. No archival images or source prose redistributed. Sources by scene: 1860: four candidates, a sectional map: https://www.archives.gov/electoral-college/1860; New Jersey breaks a simple winner map: https://www.archives.gov/electoral-college/1860; 2020: two tickets, two split states: https://www.archives.gov/electoral-college/2020; Districts inside statewide outlines: https://www.archives.gov/electoral-college/2020 Map encodes certified electoral allocation, not popular-vote share. 1860 New Jersey split Lincoln/Douglas; 2020 Maine split Biden/Trump 3/1, Nebraska 1/4. DC is shown in 2020. Neutral 1860 shapes are not-yet-admitted states; Maine, Virginia and other modern outlines differ from historical geography. Blank area is not a vote category.

scenes.title: 1860: four candidates, a sectional map
scenes.text: The National Archives records electoral votes for Lincoln, Douglas, Breckinridge and Bell. New Jersey split its electors. Colours show certified allocations on modern reference outlines, not vote shares or exact 1860 boundaries.

scenes.title: New Jersey breaks a simple winner map
scenes.text: In 1860 New Jersey appointed electors individually. Lincoln received four of its electoral votes and Douglas three; assigning the state entirely to either candidate would erase the split.

scenes.title: 2020: two tickets, two split states
scenes.text: The certified 2020 Electoral College result was Biden 306, Trump 232. Maine and Nebraska split their allocations, so the purple category distinguishes them from states assigning all electors to one ticket.

scenes.title: Districts inside statewide outlines
scenes.text: Maine allocated three votes to Biden and one to Trump; Nebraska allocated one to Biden and four to Trump. These points locate the states. This chapter does not invent district boundaries or imply proportional popular-vote representation.

scenes.title: The two noncontiguous states
scenes.text: In the certified 2020 allocation, Alaska cast its electoral votes for Trump and Hawaii for Biden. Their distant geography belongs to the electoral map even though a continental camera cannot show every state at once. Source: National Archives 2020 results.
